stories.title: President Trump Sells Micron Stock and Buys Another Mega-Cap Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock
stories.simple_summary: President Trump sold his stock in a computer chip company and bought shares in a different large company that works with artificial intelligence. This is mostly a personal investment decision by one wealthy person.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors who follow what powerful people are buying and selling. There's nothing you need to do about it.

stories.title: Why metal detecting is booming in the age of social media and AI
stories.simple_summary: Metal detecting as a hobby has become more popular, partly because people share their finds on social media and AI is helping identify what they find. The article doesn't specify how AI helps with the hobby itself.
stories.why_it_matters: If you enjoy hobbies or want to try something new, metal detecting might be more accessible now because of these tools. Otherwise this doesn't affect your daily life.

stories.title: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns
stories.simple_summary: Meta (the company behind Facebook) changed the wording in their legal agreement after people complained. The company says they didn't actually change what they do, just how they describe it.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Facebook, this means Meta is trying to be more careful about what they say they're allowed to do, though their actual practices may not have changed.

stories.title: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings
stories.simple_summary: The company Anthropic says it has hired more experienced workers and now people spend more time in meetings. This is mostly company news for investors.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors watching Anthropic. There's nothing you need to do about it.

stories.title: Replit makes OpenAI its default over Anthropic, CEO says
stories.simple_summary: Replit, a computer coding website, switched to using OpenAI's chatbot as its default choice instead of Anthropic's Claude. You can still use Claude if you want.
stories.why_it_matters: If you don't use Replit for coding, this doesn't affect you. If you do, you'll see a different AI chatbot by default when you visit the site.

stories.title: Meta removes language that may have allowed it to scrape news sites
stories.simple_summary: Meta removed certain language from its terms of service that suggested the company could copy news articles from websites without permission to train its AI. After complaints, they decided not to allow this.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own a website or write online content, this means Meta is backing off from being able to grab your work without asking. For regular people, it's a small win for protecting original content.

stories.title: CoreWeave Woes Risk Shutting Down AI Junk Market: Credit Weekly
stories.simple_summary: CoreWeave, a company that provides computer power for AI projects, is having serious financial problems that could affect the entire AI industry's equipment market. The details are unclear from the headline alone.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to companies building AI systems and investors. Most small businesses won't feel direct effects unless they rely on AI services that depend on CoreWeave's equipment.

stories.title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
stories.simple_summary: As AI companies create computer agents that can do tasks like booking reservations or shopping online by themselves, websites are starting to block these agents from visiting them. Owners want to control what the AI can see and do.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own a small business with a website, you might soon need to think about whether to allow or block AI agents from visiting your site.

stories.title: The power of AI is worrying senior Labour figures – as is the fear of ‘falling behind the public’
stories.simple_summary: British Labour party leaders are concerned that artificial intelligence could become too powerful and that they might fall behind other countries in AI technology. This is political discussion about AI policy.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to people interested in government policy. It signals that political leaders are paying attention to AI, which may lead to new rules in the future.

stories.title: China AI supply-chain IPOs hold firm despite valuation pullback, Citi says
stories.simple_summary: Chinese companies that make equipment and supplies for the AI industry are still doing well with their stock offerings, even though some prices have gone down a bit. This is mostly financial news.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors watching the Chinese tech market. It shows that AI equipment companies remain valuable despite recent market changes.

stories.title: China says it will curb tech exports, including AI, citing national security risks
stories.simple_summary: The Chinese government announced it will restrict selling AI technology and related equipment to other countries because it considers these materials important for national security. This is a trade policy decision.
stories.why_it_matters: If you run a business that relies on Chinese tech supplies, this could eventually affect your costs or availability. Most small businesses won't see immediate changes.

stories.title: India becomes the latest country to report rogue AI agent activity
stories.simple_summary: In India, hackers used rogue AI agents that got access to computer systems by finding passwords and access information that people left exposed in public places or used overly open security settings. The agents then did things the hackers wanted.
stories.why_it_matters: If you or your small business use cloud storage or web applications, this is a reminder to keep your passwords and access settings private and secure. Don't leave them in code you post publicly.
